problem: Topological neural networks rely on fixed unsupervised graph lifting operations that are chosen a priori, yet this choice critically impacts downstream task performance.
approach: DiffLift learns graph liftings end-to-end by using learned vertex-level latent representations to identify and parameterize distributions over candidate higher-order cells, enabling learnable transformations to hypergraphs and simplicial complexes.
contribution: DiffLift outperforms static lifting methods with gains up to 45% across graph and node classification benchmarks on multiple TNN architectures.

problem: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial examples, and existing empirical defenses like adversarial training and robust distillation remain limited in robustness.
approach: Nasty Adversarial Training identifies and leverages probability sparsity—sparse probability distributions induced during training—as a regularization mechanism to enhance adversarial robustness through interpretable spatial metric preferences.
contribution: NAT demonstrates theoretically grounded and empirically validated improvements in adversarial robustness through probability sparsity regularization.

problem: Diffusion Transformers suffer from prohibitive attention latency due to long sequences and quadratic complexity in video generation.
approach: SLA decouples attention weights into critical high-rank and negligible low-rank components, applying sparse attention to critical weights, linear attention to marginal weights, and skipping negligible ones via a single GPU kernel.
contribution: SLA achieves 20x reduction in attention computation and 95% reduction in attention computational cost with 13.7x attention speedup and 2.2x end-to-end video generation speedup without quality degradation.

problem: State Space Models like Mamba lack Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning methods tailored to their unique temporal processing dynamics, limiting their practical adaptation to downstream tasks.
approach: Memba combines bio-inspired Leaky Integrate Membrane neurons as gating mechanisms with Low-Rank Adaptations and cross-layer membrane transfer to enhance temporal modeling during fine-tuning.
contribution: Memba achieves substantial improvements over existing PEFT methods across language and vision tasks.

problem: Training novel Vector Quantization modules for state-of-the-art discrete visual tokenizers requires prohibitive computational resources, preventing innovation under resource constraints.
approach: VQ-Transplant enables plug-and-play integration of new VQ modules into frozen pre-trained tokenizers by replacing their native VQ modules and using lightweight decoder adaptation for only 5 epochs.
contribution: VQ-Transplant achieves near state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity while reducing training cost by 95% compared to full retraining.

problem: Weather Foundation Models require Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning but existing PEFT methods designed for vision/language fail to address unique weather task challenges like variable heterogeneity and spatiotemporal coverage variations.
approach: WeatherPEFT introduces Task-Adaptive Dynamic Prompting for context-aware feature recalibration and Stochastic Fisher-Guided Adaptive Selection to identify task-critical parameters during backpropagation.
contribution: WeatherPEFT achieves performance parity with Full-Tuning using fewer trainable parameters across three downstream weather tasks.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs with reinforcement learning faces challenges in fine-grained credit assignment from sparse sequence-end rewards and requires computationally expensive critic networks.
approach: GN-IVO learns step-level values implicitly through group-normalized distributional matching across sampled model responses, eliminating the need for explicit critics.
contribution: GN-IVO outperforms strong RL baselines on text generation and reasoning tasks without explicit critic training.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for training reasoning LLMs suffers from efficiency bottlenecks in the rollout process, which consumes up to 70% of training time.
approach: QuRL uses a quantized actor for accelerated rollout with Adaptive Clipping Range to dynamically adjust clipping ratios and invariant scaling to reduce quantization noise.
contribution: QuRL achieves 20% to 80% faster rollout during RL training with INT8 and FP8 quantization without training collapse.

problem: Spectral Graph Neural Networks achieve strong node classification performance but node distinguishability remains poorly understood and limited by eigenvalue multiplicity and feature sparsity.
approach: AdaSpec generates adaptive graph matrices that enhance node distinguishability by increasing distinct eigenvalues while preserving permutation equivariance and computational complexity.
contribution: AdaSpec improves node distinguishability of spectral GNNs across eighteen benchmark datasets.

problem: Zero-shot diffusion-based image compression methods are slow and computationally demanding despite recent progress.
approach: Turbo-DDCM efficiently combines multiple noise vectors at each denoising step using an improved encoding protocol and supports priority-aware and distortion-controlled variants.
contribution: Turbo-DDCM runs substantially faster than existing methods while maintaining state-of-the-art compression performance with flexible targeting options.

problem: Clustered Federated Learning relies solely on data or gradient similarity for clustering, missing a holistic view of client similarities and restricting knowledge sharing within clusters.
approach: FedDAG uses a weighted class-wise similarity metric integrating data and gradient information for clustering and adopts dual-encoder architectures with cross-cluster feature transfer.
contribution: FedDAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art clustered FL baselines across diverse benchmarks and data heterogeneity settings.

problem: Existing persistence diagram embeddings like persistence images and landscapes fail to preserve Wasserstein geometry in a theoretically optimal way with limited stability or geometric fidelity.
approach: Persistence spheres define a bi-continuous mapping using Lipschitz continuity with respect to 1-Wasserstein distance with an invertible image, preserving Wasserstein geometry optimally in linear space.
contribution: Persistence spheres achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance on clustering, regression, and classification across functional data, time series, graphs, meshes, and point clouds.

problem: Existing LLM benchmarks lack standardized process-aware evaluation capturing instruction adherence and process fidelity, and suffer from scarce accurately labeled training data for data science tasks.
approach: DARE-bench provides 6,300 Kaggle-derived tasks with verifiable ground truth and large-scale training data enabling objective evaluation of LLM performance on data science and machine learning modeling.
contribution: Supervised fine-tuning boosts Qwen3-32B accuracy 1.83x and reinforcement learning boosts Qwen3-4B accuracy more than 8x, demonstrating DARE-bench's value for training and evaluation.

problem: Long-horizon embodied manipulation tasks require synergistic integration of textual reasoning and visual-spatial imagination, but existing methods lack unified multimodal generation frameworks.
approach: EVLP proposes a unified multimodal generation framework integrating semantic and spatial features with dynamic pretraining and reinforced supervised fine-tuning to align spatial logic between actions and generated images.
contribution: EVLP enables effective multimodal planning for long-horizon embodied tasks through coordinated language-visual modeling.

problem: Generative video frame interpolation methods are constrained to synthesizing fixed numbers of intermediate frames, lacking flexibility in frame rates and sequence duration.
approach: ArbInterp introduces Timestamp-aware Rotary Position Embedding for fine-grained frame timestamp control and appearance-motion decoupled conditioning for seamless segment-wise synthesis across arbitrary interpolation factors.
contribution: ArbInterp supports interpolation at any timestamp and length with higher fidelity and seamless spatiotemporal continuity across 2x to 32x interpolation factors.

problem: Vision-language models excel at multimodal understanding but fail to extend effectively to embodied tasks where linguistic instructions must map to motor actions.
approach: SP-VLA leverages spatial priors as a bridge via spatial grounding pretraining on point/box/trajectory prediction and spatially guided action post-training to align action learning with spatial priors.
contribution: SP-VLA achieves 66.1→84.6 on Google Robot and 54.7→73.2 on WidowX with improved generalization to unseen objects and robustness to real-world perturbations.

problem: Speech-to-speech processing tasks like enhancement face data limitations causing generative approaches to distort content and speaker identity.
approach: SpeechOp adapts pre-trained TTS models into universal speech processors via latent diffusion and introduces Implicit Task Composition using ASR-derived transcripts to guide enhancement.
contribution: SpeechOp achieves state-of-the-art content preservation and improves core TTS performance through multi-task learning and inference-time task composition.

problem: Audio editing models depend on template-like instruction formats and operate on mono-channel audio, failing to handle declarative editing where users specify desired outcomes without operation details.
approach: SmartDJ combines audio language model reasoning with latent diffusion, decomposing high-level instructions into atomic edit operations and synthesizing stereo audio via learned cross-modal attention.
contribution: SmartDJ achieves superior perceptual quality, spatial realism, and semantic alignment for declarative stereo audio editing compared to prior methods.

problem: Existing jailbreak defenses are computationally expensive and often result in high refusal rates, hindering practical deployment of safeguards for large language models.
approach: Enhanced Constitutional Classifiers use full exchange classifiers to evaluate conversational context and employ a cascade of lightweight classifiers screening traffic to reduce costs.
contribution: The defense achieves 5.4x computational cost reduction and 0.036% refusal rate while maintaining protection against universal jailbreaks across 560K+ tested queries.

problem: Latent reasoning in LLMs suffers from critical lack of supervision, limiting effectiveness on complex natural-language reasoning traces despite efficiency benefits over verbose chain-of-thought.
approach: KaVa distills knowledge from compressed KV-cache of teacher models into latent-reasoning students via self-distillation, leveraging continuous latent tokens to align stepwise KV trajectories.
contribution: KaVa outperforms latent baselines and shows markedly smaller degradation from equation-only to natural-language reasoning while preserving efficiency.

problem: Hadamard products offer theoretical benefits for inducing nonlinear representations in deep learning but lack practical deployment in efficient vision models.
approach: Hadaptive-Net introduces the Adaptive Cross-Hadamard module with differentiable discrete sampling and dynamic softsign normalization, integrated via neural architecture search for efficient vision models.
contribution: ACH achieves state-of-the-art accuracy/speed trade-offs on image classification, establishing Hadamard operations as fundamental building blocks for efficient vision models.

problem: Style transfer methods typically operate globally and overlook region-wise and pixel-wise semantic correspondence between similar objects.
approach: CoCoDiff is a training-free framework leveraging pretrained latent diffusion models with pixel-wise semantic correspondence modules and cycle-consistency mechanisms for fine-grained stylization.
contribution: CoCoDiff delivers state-of-the-art visual quality without additional training or supervision, outperforming methods requiring extra training or annotations.

problem: Scaling imitation learning to high-DoF whole-body robots is fundamentally limited by dimensionality curse and prohibitive expert demonstration collection costs.
approach: HVD structures the value function along the robot's kinematic hierarchy and temporal chunks using Transformer architecture for multi-modal and multi-task learning from imperfect reward-labeled trajectories.
contribution: HVD significantly outperforms baselines on complex whole-body tasks and enables policy learning from realistic imperfect data rather than perfect demonstrations.

problem: Offline RL methods rely on complex planning architectures with high inference costs, hindering real-world deployment despite strong empirical results.
approach: TGCVG integrates high-performing offline policies with learned dynamics models and introduces value-guided regularization to ensure synthesized trajectories are high-quality and distribution-preserving.
contribution: TGCVG improves state-of-the-art offline RL performance while significantly reducing training and trajectory synthesis time.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning of VLAs relies on costly human demonstrations, limiting scalability and generalization to unseen tasks.
approach: PLD uses residual reinforcement learning to train lightweight specialists that probe failure regions, collects deployment-aligned trajectories biased toward frequent failure states, and distills recovery behaviors via SFT.
contribution: PLD achieves 99% task success on LIBERO and over 50% performance gains in SimplerEnv while demonstrating real-world manipulation improvements.

problem: Low-rank adaptation relies on low-rank matrices to approximate weight updates but increasing the rank to improve fine-tuning performance significantly increases trainable parameters.
approach: BoRA treats the LoRA product as block matrix multiplication with unique diagonal matrices for each block, enhancing diversity and increasing rank expressiveness while requiring only b²r additional parameters.
contribution: BoRA increases LoRA rank expressiveness by factor b with minimal parameter overhead, demonstrating superior performance across multiple datasets and models.

problem: Low-bit quantization has emerged as essential for efficient training of large models but lacks rigorous theoretical understanding of its impact on learning performance.
approach: This work provides the first systematic theoretical analysis of quantized SGD for high-dimensional linear regression under multiple quantization targets, establishing algorithm-dependent excess risk bounds.
contribution: The analysis distinguishes additive quantization effects (noise suppression scaled by batch size) from multiplicative quantization (spectral structure preservation).

problem: LLM-based recommendation systems typically rely on explicit chain-of-thought data which is difficult to obtain and incurs high inference latency.
approach: LatentR³ uses reinforcement learning with a modified GRPO algorithm to optimize latent reasoning without explicit CoT supervision, employing a two-stage training strategy with rule-based reward design.
contribution: LatentR³ enables effective latent reasoning without direct CoT supervision while reducing inference latency and improving recommendation performance.

problem: Multimodal RAG systems lack watermarking methods to protect image knowledge copyright in shared knowledge bases.
approach: AQUA embeds semantic signals into synthetic images using acronym-based triggers and spatial relationship cues that survive indirect propagation from image retriever to textual generator.
contribution: AQUA enables robust, stealthy, and reliable copyright tracing for image knowledge in multimodal RAG systems.

problem: Existing view transformers for robotic manipulation extract static visual representations lacking adequate 3D spatial reasoning and dynamic adaptation.
approach: Cortical Policy uses dual-stream design inspired by human cortex: static-view stream for spatial understanding via 3D keypoint alignment, dynamic-view stream for adaptation via egocentric gaze estimation.
contribution: Cortical Policy substantially outperforms baselines on RLBench, COLOSSEUM, and real-world manipulation tasks with language-conditional control.

problem: Inferring interpretable intrinsic dynamics from visual observations faces challenges: manually defined priors don't align with actual dynamics while neural networks lack interpretability.
approach: VisionLaw uses bilevel optimization where LLMs generate constitutive laws with decoupling mechanisms and vision-guided evaluation uses visual simulation to assess law consistency.
contribution: VisionLaw effectively infers interpretable intrinsic dynamics from visual observations with strong generalization for interactive simulation in novel scenarios.

problem: Text-to-motion generation struggles to capture temporal and causal complexities in natural language, producing oversimplified or incoherent motions.
approach: Motion-R1 combines Decomposed Chain-of-Thought reasoning with reinforcement learning via a Decomposed CoT Data Engine for synthetic reasoning data and RL Binding for text-motion alignment.
contribution: Motion-R1 achieves 3.5% improvement in MM-Dist on HumanML3D and improvements in R-Precision and FID on other benchmarks.

problem: LLMs struggle with graph understanding due to structural hallucination, existing approaches either verbalize graphs consuming excessive tokens or use soft prompts with misalignment to text tokens.
approach: <SO$G_k$> incorporates one special token fully representing graph structure via topology-aware structural tokenizer and hybrid structure Question-Answering corpora to align structural tokens with text.
contribution: <SO$G_k$> achieves 9.9–41.4% performance improvement on five graph-level benchmarks with improved interpretability and consistency for graph understanding.

problem: Large-scale text-to-image diffusion models suffer from prohibitive computational costs and existing one-shot pruning methods cannot be directly applied to their iterative denoising nature.
approach: OBS-Diff adapts classic Optimal Brain Surgeon to diffusion models with timestep-aware Hessian construction using logarithmic-decrease weighting and group-wise sequential pruning strategy.
contribution: OBS-Diff achieves state-of-the-art one-shot pruning with minimal visual quality degradation for diverse sparsity types on large-scale text-to-image models.

problem: Transformer-based language models struggle to reliably capture distant contextual information due to limited positional encoding effectiveness.
approach: Meta-tokens paired with meta-attention mechanism are injected during pre-training to sharpen positional encoding and operate as content-based anchors compressing preceding context.
contribution: Meta-tokens enable length generalization up to 2x context window extension with strong synthetic task performance and mechanistic insights into context compression.

problem: Test-time adaptation methods struggle to fully leverage large pretrained models while maintaining minimal parameter updates and addressing feature variance reduction.
approach: IMSE leverages spectral experts via singular value decomposition, adapting only singular values while keeping vectors fixed, and proposes diversity maximization based on singular vector-input alignment.
contribution: IMSE achieves state-of-the-art performance on single-domain TTA with 3.4pp improvement in CTTA using 2,000x fewer trainable parameters.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning & Lifelong Learning

problem: Open-source image editing models lag behind closed-source ones due to lack of reliable reward models to scale high-quality synthetic training data.
approach: EditReward is trained on 200K+ preference pairs annotated by experts following rigorous protocols and aligns with human preferences better than VLM-as-judge models.
contribution: EditReward achieves state-of-the-art human correlation on GenAI-Bench, AURORA-Bench, ImagenHub, and novel EditReward-Bench benchmarks.

problem: Generating 3D human poses from multimodal inputs faces alignment gaps between supervised objectives and task requirements, compromising semantic and spatial fidelity.
approach: Pose-RFT shifts from supervised imitation to reward-driven fine-tuning via HyGRPO, a hybrid RL algorithm handling joint discrete language and continuous pose optimization.
contribution: Pose-RFT significantly improves performance over existing pose-specific MLLMs on multiple benchmarks for image-to-pose and text-to-pose generation.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models for robotic manipulation face inefficient inference due to dense visual token attention dominance, especially over long-horizon multi-modal context.
approach: ADP integrates text-driven token selection with action-aware trajectory gating, conditioning pruning on past motion windows to adaptively adjust token retention across manipulation stages.
contribution: ADP achieves 1.35x speed up on OpenVLA-OFT with 25.8% improvements in success rate across LIBERO and real-world manipulation scenarios.

problem: Class-Incremental Learning assumes shared domain distribution, limiting applicability when data arrive from evolving environments requiring bidirectional domain transferability.
approach: XEED leverages domain-specialized prompts, residual-guided representation modulation, and evolving prototypes to expand class semantics across domains bidirectionally.
contribution: XEED outperforms CIL baselines significantly on standard accuracy and novel BiDoT metrics for continual learning under domain-evolving conditions.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning & Lifelong Learning
